objective: Measure the spatial block size, channel response, and resolution scaling of ArtifactFilmGrungeEffect grainAmount/grainSize using its source equations, without claiming product-path parity or perceptual acceptance.

scope.effect: ArtifactFilmGrungeEffect grain equation only; grainAmount=0.075, seed=1977, frame=0. All other controls set to zero so warp/exposure/vignette/stain/scratch/dust are neutral.
scope.method: Independent NumPy float32 model of the intended low-32-bit grain hash and positive std::round-equivalent grainBlock mapping. In the current C++ expression, x/y integer products occur in signed int before uint32 cast and can overflow; that is undefined by C++, so this model assumes common modulo-2^32 wrap and does not claim compiled-source parity.
excluded: C++ compiled output and std::mt19937 behavior (the grain hash itself is deterministic and does not use MT draws)
approval of visual quality, emulsion physics, or matched strength to other effects
temporal changes beyond the fixed frame 0 condition
GPU/preview/final parity, performance, memory, and runtime allocation

comparison.baseline: Same synthetic/photo source plate with grainAmount=0; paired subtraction identifies the modeled grain field.
comparison.candidates: grainSize requests [1.0, 1.25, 1.49, 1.5, 1.51, 2.49, 2.5, 2.51, 4.0, 8.0] at fixed grainAmount .075, seed 1977, frame 0.
comparison.ground_truth: None. Source formula is the implementation reference; no approved grain appearance reference exists.
comparison.acceptance: Only model invariants are gates. Report requested size and rounded block size separately; report source signed-overflow risk. No perceptual ranking, parameter equivalence, or quality pass/fail.

materials.source: In-script 1024x1024 opaque chart: low/mid/high flat bands, fine lines, checker patch and gradient.

conditions.resolution: 512x512 and 1024x1024; each 512 plate is LANCZOS downsampled from its paired 1024 plate.
conditions.numeric_domain: RGB float32 normalized values. The source photograph's sRGB-decoded-by-file RGB8 values are normalized and used directly; no transfer conversion is applied. This does not establish the product working-space contract.
conditions.alpha: Opaque alpha 1.0; input/output alpha identity is an arithmetic invariant only.
conditions.frame_seed: seed=1977, compositionFrame=0; exact source frameSeed equation is used.
conditions.measurement: Per-channel grain residual mean/std/RMS/min/max, clipping excursion counts, unique hash levels, same-row/column lag correlation, exact within-block constancy, and display-only contact sheets plus selected 1:1 center crops.
conditions.display: PNG uses direct numeric RGB clipped to [0,1] and quantized to RGB8; these diagnostic PNG values are not the product Viewer transform. Raw float metrics remain authoritative.

effect_correctness.method: Verify source markers, intended low-32-bit arithmetic model, positive std::round-equivalent block rounding, fixed-seed determinism, grainAmount=0 identity, and exact shared residual within each block. Record float32 output-minus-input roundtrip error separately.
effect_correctness.acceptance_criteria: Exact agreement with the declared Python model, finite values, output-minus-input residual roundtrip within one float32 ULP of the source magnitude, and explicit C++ signed-overflow caveat. No image-quality gate.

image_quality_and_detail.method: Compare raw grain residual distributions and inspect full images / 1:1 center crops at fixed display conditions.
image_quality_and_detail.acceptance_criteria: No aesthetic acceptance; describe source-model response only.

color_and_alpha.method: Record per-channel residual scale, unclamped range, RGB alpha passthrough on opaque inputs.
color_and_alpha.acceptance_criteria: Do not generalize alpha behavior to translucent edges or RGB response to a different working space.

temporal_stability.reason: Fixed frame 0 only; a separate actual frame sequence is required.

render_paths_and_resolution.method: Compare two still resolutions in the source-equation model.
render_paths_and_resolution.unverified: Registered CPU invocation, preview/final, GPU, and backend parity.

execution.thresholds: No perceptual thresholds. Invariant gates are exact float-array repeatability within this Python process, alpha identity, finite output, and formula-derived block constancy.
execution.reproducibility: Record plan/source/script/input hashes, Python/NumPy/Pillow versions, all requested/rounded sizes, metrics JSON and checksum.

amendments.reason: Review after the initial model run found that the C++ hash multiplies signed ints before casting to uint32. Those products exceed INT32_MAX for parts of the tested images, making C++ behavior undefined despite the intended low-32-bit hash interpretation.
amendments.change: Narrow model claims to explicit modulo-2^32 intended arithmetic, record signed-overflow risk per condition, and rerun the full comparison against this amended plan.
amendments.scope_effect: No materials, candidate grainSize values, or descriptive metrics changed; compiled parity is explicitly disclaimed.

amendments.reason: Float32 output addition followed by output-minus-input subtraction incurs one-ULP rounding even when the modeled grain field is correct.
amendments.change: Report the roundtrip error and use a one-float32-ULP invariant bound instead of requiring exact subtraction recovery; rerun the complete report.
amendments.scope_effect: This changes only a numerical invariant, not the effect, inputs, candidate parameters, or image-quality criteria.
